t: It is already done | WordReference Forums
s: November 2, 2018 - Since the moment of speaking is the "present," the tense of the auxiliary can be the "present tense." The auxiliary can be one word (It is already done, where present tense is marked by "is") or more than one word (It has already been done, "has been" = periphrastic construction, where present tense is marked by "has").
